transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Start: 08:34 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Celestia Head of Legal), Priya (Procurement), Marcus (CTO), Devon (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining. Maya Patel from Redwood, I'll kick us off. We have Liam from SE and Sofia from CSM on the call. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jordan: Morning. Doing well, thanks. Big agenda today is the MSA and DPA redlines and the SLA appendix, and then touch on pricing for the pilot.
[00:15] Priya: Yep, procurement side - we need to check the standard vendor onboarding checklist and any risk items.
[00:20] Liam: Great. We'll go through the redlines you've shared, and then I can cover the technical bits on KMS, VPC/private deployment options, and how our dedicated pools and hosted API affect SLAs and data controls.

[00:32] Jordan: To set expectations, legal is looking at indemnity, liability caps, data breach notification timelines, and data residency clauses. Also we flagged KMS/HSM integration and whether keys can be customer-managed.
[00:42] Maya: Understood. We typically support a couple of patterns: hosted with Redwood-managed keys, or Private with customer-managed KMS or HSM depending on the deployment. Liam, want to briefly summarise?
[00:50] Liam: Sure. For hosted we can offer envelope encryption with customer KMS in some regions; for Private we provide a customer-controlled key integration pattern. HSM-level key custody needs an on-prem or VPC private deployment with our private control plane - that path satisfies most enterprise HSM requirements. There's some ops work and network configuration.

[01:07] Devon: When you say "customer-managed KMS" - is that AWS KMS cross-account or bring-your-own HSM? We need to know the auth flows and whether the KMS key material is ever in Redwood's environment.
[01:18] Liam: Good question. For cross-account KMS, Redwood doesn't store key material; we call the customer's KMS to decrypt tokens. For HSM, typically the key never leaves the HSM and operations are orchestrated in your VPC. We'll send the integration notes.

[01:36] Jordan: Liability language - your team sent an alternative cap that references gross negligence; we typically need explicit carveouts for willful misconduct but want a higher overall cap for security incidents. Can you explain your standard position?
[01:48] Maya: Our standard MSA has a liability cap tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months; we can discuss incremental increases for enterprise terms. For security incidents we do carve out willful misconduct from limitations, and we have breach notification SLA commitments. We can put proposed language in the redline.

[02:07] Marcus: On SLAs, procurement wants uptime and latency commitments. For our use case we need 99.9% for inference endpoints and p50 latency sub-500ms for text generation. Is that something you can commit to on hosted?
[02:21] Liam: Hosted tiers have published latency profiles that depend on model choice and seq length. We guarantee 99.9% for the Dedicated plan with SLA credits; hosted API has a commercial SLO, but Dedicated gives the backed SLA. For latency, p50 sub-500ms is achievable with smaller models and right batching profile; with longer contexts or larger models p50 will be higher. We can include an SLA appendix that maps model families + config to expected latency bands.

[02:52] Priya: For procurement we need the SLA credits method and the remedies - are credits the sole remedy? Many teams want more than credits for critical outages.
[03:01] Maya: Standard is service credits, not direct damages. We can discuss escalation channels and dedicated support add-on if you need faster incident response.

[03:12] Jordan: We also have a DPA question - retention and deletion timelines. We process PII in transcripts and need 30-day deletion guarantee and audit log showing deletion.
[03:22] Liam: Our platform supports configurable retention; for hosted we can enable automatic purge policies and provide audit logs showing deletion events. For Private deployments, the customer controls retention fully. We'll provide sample audit logs.

[03:37] Devon: Audit logs - what do those look like? Do they include token-level traces? We need to ensure there's no accidental data leakage in logs.
[03:45] Liam: Logs capture request IDs, timestamps, model used, and high-level metadata; by default they do not include full prompt/response text unless you enable debug logging. We can deliver sanitized audit logs for compliance reviews.

[03:58] Jordan: Great. Two other items - SSO/SAML and RBAC. Our identity team requires SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO.
[04:06] Sofia: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning; RBAC supports role templates and fine-grained permissions. We can share the admin guide.

[04:18] Priya: From procurement standpoint, payment terms - Net 60 is our standard; trial pilot pricing needs to be approved by finance. Are you flexible on pilot discounts?
[04:27] Maya: Yes, pilot discounts are negotiable depending on committed usage. We can propose a pilot SOW with a discounted rate for the first 3 months and include usage thresholds. Sofia will draft that after this call.

[04:40] Jordan: There was a clause about subcontractors - we need to list major subprocessors and their data handling practices.
[04:46] Liam: We'll share a subprocessors list and subprocessors FAQ; we have standard contracts with cloud providers and third-party logging/backups.

[05:00] Jordan: Okay let's walk through a couple redline items we sent. Item 1: Data breach notification - your 72-hour timeline is tight. We prefer 48 hours if possible for incidents that materially affect PII.
[05:11] Maya: Our standard is notification within 72 hours after confirming the incident, to avoid false positives. I can flag this as negotiable; we can add a clause for expedited notice for confirmed material exposures.

[05:25] Jordan: Next, the audit right - we want annual SOC2-like audit evidence and the right to request up to one third-party audit every 24 months.
[05:34] Liam: We publish SOC2 reports and ISO attestation; customers can request more through our security team. Third-party audit rights often require more controls around scope, but we can surface our security pack and discuss a mutually agreeable approach.

[05:46] Marcus: On the tech side, if we do a Dedicated pool, what's the expected lead time to stand it up for pilot? We need it ASAP to run performance tests.
[05:56] Liam: For Dedicated - provisioning typically takes 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and region. If you can be flexible, we also offer burst capacity on hosted with reserved lanes for short-term stress tests.

[06:12] Devon: We have a secondary question - do you store model weights or do you operate in a model marketplace fashion where weights are pulled? Specifically for IP concerns.
[06:20] Liam: We host and serve model variants on our runtime; model weights are stored in Redwood-managed artifact stores. For Private/on-prem we can arrange an onboarding where the customer brings a model artifact. We can discuss an IP handling appendix if that's necessary.

[06:38] Jordan: Liability cap again - can you provide a numeric example? If last twelve months' fees are zero (pilot) the cap becomes small - we want fixed minimums for data incidents.
[06:48] Maya: Yes, for pilots we can agree to a minimum monetary cap for security liabilities and set a floor in the MSA. We'll propose language.

[07:00] Priya: Contract duration - we usually sign a 12-month term with auto-renew. Are you aligned on that or prefer month-to-month?
[07:08] Maya: For pilots it's typically a 3-month pilot SOW and then standard 12-month or annual commit for Dedicated. We'll make the SOW explicit about dates and termination rights.

[07:20] Jordan: SLA credits calculation - want to ensure credits are meaningful. How are credits applied?
[07:26] Maya: Credits are applied against future invoices; percentage tied to downtime brackets. We'll include the SLA appendix showing thresholds and credit percentages.

[07:35] Marcus: For us, performance and cost tradeoff matters. If we go Dedicated we pay more but get predictable latency and higher throughput. Can Redwood run a quick benchmark with our representative prompts?
[07:46] Liam: Absolutely. We can run a benchmark - we'll need a sample prompt set and expected concurrency. We can run on hosted first and then on a Dedicated pool when provisioned.

[07:58] Priya: On procurement approvals, we need a pricing sheet that shows pilot discount, expected monthly costs at thresholds, and the SLA appendix to route to finance.
[08:07] Sofia: We'll put together a pricing sheet and an SOW for the pilot.

[08:15] Jordan: A quick note on DPA: we want explicit language about subprocessors and 3rd-country transfers - Celestia requires EU data to stay in EU. Is regional hosting available?
[08:26] Liam: Yes, we support regional hosting for data residency in EU regions. We can commit to EU-only processing for EU tenants on our Dedicated or Private deployment. For hosted we have EU regions - we'll note that in the DPA.

[08:38] Devon: Encryption at rest and in transit details? What ciphers, TLS versions?
[08:43] Liam: TLS 1.2+ (we support 1.3 preferred), AES-256 at rest, and customer-managed KMS for key wrapping. We'll provide a short security spec.

[08:55] Jordan: Perfect. Let's talk schedule - what's the timeline for documents and approvals so procurement can put this in their queue?
[09:02] Priya: We need final MSA and DPA by next week to get legal review, otherwise our next procurement window pushes to mid-September. Net 60, finance sign-off, and compliance review are gates.

[09:12] Maya: We'll prioritize. We'll aim to get redlined MSA, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and pilot SOW to you by 2026-09-06.

[09:18] Jordan: Good. A couple of nitpicks - IP indemnity and data return/secure deletion on termination.
[09:24] Maya: We'll include a data return clause and a certificate of deletion process in the DPA. For IP, we stand by customer's data and have standard IP indemnity language - we can highlight it in the redline.

[09:36] Marcus: One more on monitoring - we want per-route metrics exported to our Prometheus stack; is that possible?
[09:42] Liam: We have metrics export options and tracing hooks; direct Prometheus scraping can be done in Private, for hosted we support pushing metrics or an integration. We'll include integration notes.

[09:55] Jordan: Anything else from Redwood?
[09:58] Sofia: Just to confirm contact points - procurement: Priya, legal: Jordan, security: Devon, tech: Marcus, and we'll coordinate with Maya and Liam on artifacts.

[10:10] Priya: Onboarding checklist - we need: SOC2, DPA, MSA, SLA appendix, pilot pricing, and technical runbook.
[10:17] Maya: We'll deliver those.

[10:20] Jordan: Recap and next steps?
[10:23] Maya: Recap: Redwood will produce a redlined MSA addressing liability cap floor and breach notice timing; we'll also include subprocessors list, sample audit logs, SOC2/ISO artifacts, pilot SOW and pricing, and KMS/HSM integration notes. Action items and due dates we'll send after call.

[10:38] Marcus: OK thanks, we'll review the redline and get finance in the loop.
[10:42] Priya: Thanks everyone.

[10:44] Jordan: Thanks. Looking forward to the artifacts.

[10:47] Maya: Thank you. We'll follow up via email with attachments and a proposed kickoff date.

[46:00] End of call

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had occasional name mismatches and some dropped punctuation; technical terms captured but sometimes spelled differently (e.g., "K M S" vs "KMS").
